text:
Priya Menon: Quick doc sync 026-03: updating the rate/quotas guide to show the new tiered metering behavior and how burst credits apply across queued requests. Need: tiny curl + python SDK snippets that include the new v2 metering header, an embed iframe for the updated "Consumption by Tier" dashboard panel, and wording sign-off for the "when credits are applied" sentence.
Alex Chen: I can draft the snippets. prefer concise curl + a requests-based python example. Should we show the fallback header for older tenants?
Priya Menon: yes include fallback example using `x-metering-legacy` and a one-line note about quoting in shells. Also add a small comment about token granularity in the python snippet output parsing.
Jordan Lee: Dashboard moved last night. New public link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/usage/consumption-tiers. Use panelId=panel-ct-42. iframe: ```<iframe src=\"https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/usage/consumption-tiers?panelId=panel-ct-42\" width=\"100%\" height=\"400\"></iframe>```
Samir Patel: wording suggestion: replace "burst credits consumed on submit" with "burst credits are applied when the request finishes successfully". Also clarify that if a queued request times out, reserved credits are released back to the bucket.
Priya Menon: good change. I'll adopt "applied when the request completes successfully". Add a short example table showing events: request_start, request_complete(success|timeout), credits_delta.
Alex Chen: snippet draft below. Keeping it minimal for docs.
Alex Chen: ```bash
# curl example (minimal)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Metering: {\"client_id\":\"team-17\",\"job_id\":\"j-2026-03-01\"}" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd/latency-optimized","input":"Explain the quota change."}'
```
Alex Chen: ```python
# python requests example
import os
import requests
headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "X-Redwood-Metering": '{"client_id":"team-17","job_id":"j-2026-03-01"}'
}
payload = {"model": "rwd/latency-optimized", "input": "Explain the quota change."}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json().get('usage', {}))  # tokens and meter_rate fields shown here
```
Alex Chen: fallback header example: `-H "x-metering-legacy: client=team-17"`
Priya Menon: add the one-line note about escaping quotes: "Note: when copying the X-Redwood-Metering header into some shells, escape double quotes or use single-quoted header values."
Maria Gonzales: I'll prep the Spanish translation for the new sentence: "los créditos de ráfaga se aplican cuando la solicitud finaliza correctamente". Also check pluralization for "tokens" in the usage table.
Samir Patel: minor: in the usage table use columns "event | credits_delta | note" and show example rows. Also mention the retention period for meter records (30 days) somewhere near the table.
Priya Menon: great. I'm going to open a tiny PR now: #3510 docs/rate-meters/snippet-and-embed. Assigning: Alex for code, Jordan for dashboard iframe check, Samir for behavior wording, Maria for l10n. DocBot: please flag this PR for 48h review if still unapproved.
DocBot: Reminder set: will post a follow-up in #docs in 48 hours if PR #3510 has no approvals. :robot_face:
Alex Chen: pushing the branch with snippets in ~5m and will ping here when the PR is up.
Priya Menon: thanks team 1 I'll merge after L10n + Jordan verify iframe renders in staging.
